title: Shot bucketization and KV cacheline coalescer for compact prompt memoization
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Small, repeated few-shot prompts cause heavy KV duplication across requests (many near-identical short context windows). The existing prefix-dedup approaches detect exact fingerprint matches but struggle with semantically similar few-shot variations and suffer GPU memory fragmentation when storing many small fragments. Continuous batching increases co-location of such requests but does not reduce per-request KV residency.

Goal: Implement a two-part system that (1) groups short-context requests into 'shot buckets' based on lightweight semantic hashing and template alignment so they can share canonicalized KV fragments, and (2) modify the GPU KV allocator with a cacheline coalescer that packs many small fragments into contiguous slab segments to reduce fragmentation and per-fragment overhead. The expected outcome is a measurable drop in peak GPU KV memory and overall GPU residency while maintaining end-to-end latency SLOs and no degradation in token-level quality for canonicalized prompts.

Scope: Backend runtime changes only (inference serving runtime + allocator). No API changes. Work covers hashing/bucketing heuristics, canonicalization rules, coalescer allocator, fallbacks for non-canonicalizable prompts, metrics and dashboards, and canary rollout logic.
acceptance_criteria: Server can classify incoming short-context requests (<128 input tokens) into shot buckets with <= 5ms classification overhead per request at p95
For a representative production trace, peak KV GPU memory reduces by >= 20% compared to baseline when shot buckets enabled
End-to-end 95th percentile generation latency increases by < 5% for cached workloads and by < 10% for mixed workloads
No observable change in model output quality for canonicalized prompts (auto-eval regression < 0.5% on our synthetic few-shot prompt set)
Allocator telemetry added: slab utilization, coalesced-fragment-count, fragmentation-ratio, and per-tenant soft-quota hits
Feature gated with runtime flag and rollout canary that can revert to prior behavior without requiring model reloads
design_notes: Shot bucketing approach uses a two-stage fingerprint: (a) template-normalize by stripping variable slots (timestamps, IDs, whitespace/quote normalization), (b) locality-sensitive hashing (SimHash 64-bit) over tokens after stopword-insensitive tokenization. This yields ~90% precision on a small audit set for grouping similar few-shot templates.

Canonicalization policy: preserve literal content in answer slots, canonicalize instruction wording and few-shot example ordering where safe. Provide tunable aggression levels (conservative, balanced, aggressive) behind flags.

Coalescer allocator: instead of allocating tiny independent GPU slabs per fragment, allocate 4KB-64KB 'micro-slabs' and pack canonicalized fragments compactly with an index. Micro-slabs are backed by nucleated free lists and support refcounting at fragment granularity to allow safe eviction and reuse.

Interplay with continuous batching: classification happens on request ingest; similar requests arriving in the same batch are grouped to reference the same coalesced KV region. This reduces per-batch KV copy overhead and leverages cross-request KV reuse during synchronous generation passes.
Fallback: if canonicalization fails or the fragment is too unique, fall back to existing per-request KV path to avoid correctness risks. Metrics track fallback rate.
Security: canonicalization is deterministic and runs in-memory without storing user textual content to disk; however, we add an opt-out with tenant policy for PII-sensitive tenants.
Rollout: start with 'conservative' canonicalization for 10% of traffic lanes (internal + low-traffic customers), observe quality, then expand aggression and traffic.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Instrumentation and data sampling - add lightweight fingerprinting to prod sampling agent and gather 7 days of short-context requests for bucket modeling (owner: Arjun)
Week 2: Build canonicalizer prototype and offline clustering tool to validate bucketing precision/recall on sampled traces (owner: Elena)
Week 3: Implement allocator coalescer micro-slab APIs and internal refcounted fragment index (owner: Kyle)
Week 4: Integrate shot classification into request ingress path and connect canonicalizer to allocator write path (owner: Arjun + Kyle)
Week 5: Add metrics, dashboards, and canary flag. End-to-end load test with mixed workloads (owner: SRE: Priya)
Week 6: Canary rollout and progressive traffic ramp if metrics meet acceptance criteria (owner: Eng + Product)
PRs: initial allocator patch, canonicalizer library, ingress classification hook, telemetry additions. Each PR must include unit+integration tests and release notes.
risks: Canonicalization may accidentally normalize content that affects model outputs in edge cases. Mitigation: conservative default and automatic rollback threshold based on auto-eval metrics.
Allocator bugs could cause GPU memory corruption. Mitigation: thorough unit and fuzz tests, canary on internal infra first, runtime guard pages for coalesced slabs during early rollout.

Classification overhead could increase tail latency if executed synchronously during ingress. Mitigation: keep classifier extremely lightweight (hash + small token window) and allow async warm-up for non-critical lanes.
Per-tenant differences: multi-tenant workloads might exhibit poor sharing. Mitigation: tenant-aware bucketing and soft quotas to avoid noisy-tenant eviction.
Observability gaps: if metrics are insufficient we may not detect regressions quickly. Mitigation: add explicit alarms for fragmentation ratio, fallback-rate, and auto-eval regression.
testing_plan: Unit tests: canonicalizer normalization cases, SimHash collisions bounds, allocator micro-slab refcounting correctness
Integration: end-to-end inference test that verifies identical outputs for canonicalized vs raw path on conservative set, and fallback correctness for unique prompts
Load test: replay 100k short-context requests using production traffic shape; measure peak GPU KV memory, p95 latency, and fallback rate
Canary: enable for internal and 1% external traffic; monitor auto-eval, dashboards, and error budgets for 48 hours before ramp
Regression harness: add test to nightly perf job that asserts no greater than 10% p95 latency regression for mixed workloads and at least 15% reduction in peak KV memory on saved trace
